title: RANT: Debunking the WORST pro-PED argument I hear constantly
summary: NH attacks the argument that PEDs are safe because some old bodybuilders who used them are still alive in their 70s. He points to survivorship bias, the rarity of success and income in bodybuilding, elite medical care the famous can afford, social media hiding tragedies, the 'pre-existing condition' excuse, and the fact that dying at 70 is itself early.

claims.claim: The argument that PEDs aren't dangerous because some users are still alive in their 70s is idiotic on many levels.
The 70-year-old ex-users we still see are the rare successful ones who made a career from bodybuilding; very few reach that level.
An impressive drug-built physique guarantees no income; many pro-card holders still need side jobs, and countless people with insane physiques never become known.
Famous older PED users survived partly thanks to top-level medical care and drugs costing thousands that ordinary users won't have.
Organ damage is common with PED use; if your liver fails without money or connections for a quick transplant, you die.
You hear about bodybuilders dying on stage, but not about those battling disease for 10 years or on dialysis after 5 years of PEDs, because nobody shares that on social media.
Social media shows only the best parts of lives and every post has an agenda (e.g. fat/ripped before-after to sell a supplement or plan), which makes tragedy invisible.

He predicts the YouTube/Instagram fitness scene will be completely different in 5 years because many famous PED users will stop by choice, be forced to stop, or have lifelong health problems, and they will quietly disappear.
When one enhanced influencer drops out a new one takes their place, so followers never see what happens behind the scenes.
For every PED user who reaches 70 there are, in his view, something like 49 others who are sick for life or dead and never heard from.

When users get sick or die people blame irresponsible dosing or a 'pre-existing condition'; he argues PEDs find the weak spot in the armor, and that person might have lived healthily to 80-90 without them.
A seemingly healthy 70-year-old ex-user may be sick or on lifelong medication but hide it for sponsors or pride, to protect his legacy.
With modern medicine and diet knowledge, a lifelong trainee dying at 70 is a tragedy; people should live to 80-85 in good health and physically active.
His ancestors lived long without his advantages; he would be ashamed not to at least match them and wants to be healthy for longer.
